process_observations.observation: The plan bound every required input of the borrowed agent explicitly, so nothing had to be inferred from the step title — the W08 note records that this was a deliberate fix.
The launch brief and plan.json agreed on every bound value, so no Step 5 source conflict arose; the two named artefacts to read first were the same ones depends_on already pointed at.

apex-builder has no build-layer contract — grep for artefact/build_dir/step_id/.sfskills over its AGENT.md returns 0 — so the artefact path is a request it happens to honour rather than a clause it owes; every run of this step depends on that.
deploy-order.md is written by four steps of this build and declared by none of them, which means the file a human reads before deploying is the one check-outputs never confirms.
The owning agent recorded a P1 finding that the plan settles the completion mechanism but not the completion signal, which is a question the runner cannot adjudicate and the M4 gate has to.

The step's templates[] names templates/apex/TriggerHandler.cls, but no step in this build deploys it or its TriggerControl dependency, so a template the plan told the agent to read is one it could not use.
